output:
Run 2 completed with a full report. It closes out the second-model leg — and it corrects the remedy I proposed for finding #1.

## Second-model result

`.reviews/codex-review-20260827-194911.md` — verdict **BLOCK**, covering all 15 files / ~700 non-test lines. Its **sole** critical finding is my finding #1, same location (`issue-board-backfill.mjs:144`), reached by independent reproduction. It reported nothing at any lower tier. Per the combining rule, the agreement raises confidence and prominence only — severity and the verdict are unchanged.

It did not surface findings #2 or #3; those remain confirmed by my own execution against the real parser, not withdrawn.

## Correction to the fix for finding #1

My suggested remedy — detect `Released agent claim:` comments and require the claim to postdate the newest one — is **insufficient**. `commentOnIssue` (`issue-board-commands.mjs:92-93`) returns early when `options.comment` is false, and `--no-comment` (`issue-board-cli.mjs:172-174`) is accepted by `release`. So `pnpm issue:release --issue 901 --no-comment` clears all four ownership fields and leaves **no marker at all** in the comment stream. Comment-derived staleness detection would still resurrect the stale claim on that path.

Codex's remedy is the correct one and I'm adopting it: derive the current claim epoch from the **issue timeline** (the most recent `agent-active` label-addition event), require the selected claim comment to postdate it, fail closed when no valid claim exists inside that epoch, and preserve the boundary once the issue has moved on to `in-pr`. That is a larger fix than I first implied — it needs a new paginated timeline read, with the same fail-closed pagination guards as the two readers this commit already added.

Its suggested regression cases are worth taking as-is:
- claim A → release → new `agent-active` → malformed/missing claim B ⇒ reject, write nothing
- claim A → release → valid claim B ⇒ select only B
- B then moves to `in-pr` ⇒ still associates B with its preceding `agent-active` transition
- incomplete timeline pagination ⇒ fail closed

## Coverage now

The second-model leg is a full pass, no longer partial. Run 1's 0-byte report was a timeout artifact; run 2 wrote a complete report against the same pinned commit, so both examined the correct state.

Still outstanding, unchanged: nothing exercised the live GitHub GraphQL API (date-field shape, real `authorAssociation` values, mutation ordering), and the quality-gate shell suite was not run — codex stopped it after two minutes of no output, so neither of us has coverage there.

**Verdict stands: does not pass.** Findings 1 and 2 must-fix; #1 is now a somewhat larger change than my first estimate. No files changed.
other_review:
The backfill rejects valid claim-comment forms and can leave stale ownership values after a competing-claim race. These defects affect the command's primary recovery path.

Full review comments:

- [P1] Allow branchless claim comments to backfill other fields — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1982-ee739b414256/scripts/pr/issue-board-backfill.mjs:119-119
  When `getGitBranch()` returns an empty string, such as in a detached-HEAD cloud checkout, `buildClaimComment` omits `Branch:`. This validator then rejects the entire legitimate claim, so `Agent`, `Claim ID`, and `Claimed At` cannot be recovered. Treat an absent branch as optional and exclude it from writes and conflict checks.

- [P2] Revalidate ownership before each field write — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1982-ee739b414256/scripts/pr/issue-board-backfill.mjs:264-269
  When a newer MCP claim arrives after `beforeWrite` but before this multi-field mutation finishes, the command writes the older claim into every empty field. Final verification then fails, but the stale non-empty values make later backfills fail with conflicts and require manual clearing. Re-read the lifecycle, newest claim, item schema, and values before each single-field mutation; this race is material because the MCP path has no Claim ID guard (`docs/notes/github-tooling-surfaces.md:102-110`).

- [P2] Ignore trailing newlines in handoff text — /Users/chapati/.cache/mento-review-eval/fx-1982-ee739b414256/scripts/pr/issue-board-backfill.mjs:112-112
  When a helper claim includes the Project handoff sentence and ends with a normal newline, `split("\n")` leaves a final empty element in this slice. `isBoundedCloudHandoff` rejects that element, so the command reports no valid trusted claim. Remove only trailing empty lines before validating the bounded handoff.
